title: Per-route compactor recommendations and transactional rollback playbook
creator: Asha Mehta
description: Implement a per-route 'compactor' recommendation engine that proposes batching and KV-prefetch profiles per customer and per-route, coupled with a transactional apply/rollback system and an operational playbook for safe rollouts. The goal is to surface near-term cost savings while guaranteeing recoverability if model quality or latency regressions occur.
acceptance_criteria: Compactor service produces per-route recommendations (batch_size, max_window_ms, kv_prefetch_ttl) for >=90% of active routes in staging within 24h of deployment
Recommendations include an estimated token-cost delta and a confidence score derived from traffic histograms and tail-latency distributions
Transactional apply supports atomic multi-key updates with a dry-run mode that validates rollout impact using historical traces
Automated rollback triggers on predefined SLO breaches (p50/p95 latency increase, error-rate spike, or quality metric loss) and completes revert within configured SLA
Runbook for manual rollback published and linked from Console; can execute revert via single CLI command or console action
End-to-end tests (unit + canary) exercising apply -> canary -> rollback complete in CI with synthetic workloads
proposal_summary: Build a lightweight service (compactor-service) that consumes route usage histograms, model-variant profiles, and recent evals. Score candidate profiles by cost reduction and risk. Store recommendations in a versioned policy store. Apply changes with an orchestration layer that writes change transactions and coordinates a staged canary with metric guards; provide a dry-run path that replays requests against the new profile and compares outputs/latency before committing.
implementation_notes: Data collection: extend route-telemetry ingestion to include per-request sequence length distribution, model-variant, and prefix cache hit rates
Scoring: cost_estimate = tokens * model_cost_per_token * batch_efficiency_factor; risk_estimate based on tail-latency delta and eval quality regression probability
Policy store: append-only, versioned entries keyed by (customer_id, route_id). Each entry includes suggested_profile, confidence, and dry_run_snapshot_id
Apply orchestration: transactional commit with canary slices (by customer tier and region) and timeboxed observation windows
Dry-run mechanism: replay recorded traces through runtime with candidate profile in isolated sandbox; compare outputs for semantic divergence and latency histogram shifts
Console integration: UI card showing predicted savings, confidence, and a one-click 'schedule canary' flow
Metrics: add 'compactor.apply.*' and 'compactor.rollback.*' telemetry, and SLO guardbooks referencing p50/p95/quality metrics
rollback_plan: Primary: automated rollback when any SLO guard crosses threshold for 5 minutes (p95 latency +20% over baseline OR error-rate +0.5% absolute)
Transactional revert: apply orchestration writes inverse transaction to policy store and triggers immediate canary of revert
Fallback: if automated revert fails, runbook step-by-step (1) pause traffic to affected canary, (2) run manual revert CLI (compactorctl revert --tx <id>), (3) notify on-call and kick incident channel
Reconstruction: keep dry_run_snapshot and replay traces to generate audit artifacts for postmortem
Post-rollback verification: run smoke calls across affected routes and validate latency/quality back to pre-apply baselines
tests: Unit tests for scoring logic with synthetic histograms
Integration tests: compactor-service -> policy-store -> runtime dry-run loop in staging
Canary test: 3-stage canary 1% -> 10% -> 100% with metric guards and automatic rollback simulated
Perf regression test: ensure no >5% tail latency regression in staging for common models
Chaos test: simulate KV-store transient errors during apply and verify transactional semantics hold
